invariant_hypotheses: reserved equals sum of reservations qty for the event
reserved_v2 is null or equals reserved
proposals.rationale: v1 reserve only writes reserved and relies on trigger to sync reserved_v2; backfill SELECTs reserved without lock then conditionally writes reserved_v2. Concurrent v1 increment between backfill read and write leaves trigger with OLD reserved_v2 NULL so no sync, then backfill installs stale value causing reserved != reserved_v2 permanently.

proposals.rationale: v1 release decrements reserved while trigger only syncs if reserved_v2 already non-null. If release commits after backfill read but before backfill write, backfill overwrites with stale larger value. Final reserved reflects delete but reserved_v2 does not, exposing lost decrement and divergence between dual counters.

invariant_hypotheses: reserved equals sum of reservations qty for the event
reserved >= 0 and second release must not double-decrement
proposals.rationale: Two mixed-version releases of same reservation id race on DELETE plus read-modify-write of counters. v1 path updates reserved and relies on trigger for reserved_v2 while v2 path updates both explicitly. If neither checks DELETE rowcount, both decrement counters causing double-decrement, negative drift, and reserved != sum qty.

proposals.rationale: Event near capacity with reserved_v2 NULL tests mixed capacity checks plus backfill. v1 checks reserved while v2 may check reserved_v2 which is NULL and treat NULL as 0/allow, so concurrent v1+v2 reserves that together exceed capacity can both succeed. Backfill interleaving can also install stale counter making checks diverge and hide overbooking.
